admission_edge.activation_condition: When the abstract framework has become a comfortable lens that forces incoming evidence to conform rather than updating the model when reality diverges
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Described as 'a primary antagonist' — corrupts abstraction when the framework forces reality to fit the model ('torture reality so that it fits your models') rather than revising the model to fit reality.
admission_edge.source_description: Theory-induced-blindness corrupts abstraction when the framework becomes a cage that forces reality to fit the model rather than revising the model to fit reality.
Abstraction conflicts with first-principles-thinking when high-level labels hide untested assumptions that should have been stripped away before synthesis.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When complex systems need to be compressed into clearer structures for communication or action without losing essential relationships
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Framed as an output aptitude of abstraction — 'find simplicity in complexity' — rather than a mechanism that strengthens abstraction itself. The relationship flows from abstraction producing simplification, not simplification powering abstraction.
admission_edge.source_description: Simplification is the practical expression of abstraction when complexity is compressed into a clearer structure without losing what matters.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When the listener has prior expectations or preferences that could filter incoming information toward confirming existing assumptions rather than absorbing the speaker's actual meaning
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Direct opposition — 'drives people to selectively focus only on what they want to hear' while active listening 'demands the opposite: an active openness to new ideas and data' — specific mechanism targeting the core of what listening requires.
admission_edge.source_description: Confirmation-bias blocks active-listening when incoming information is filtered to support what the listener already wants to believe.
Active-listening conflicts with optimization-theory when pure metric optimization suppresses trust-building dialogue required for alignment.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When information gathered through listening needs to be evaluated for facts vs. assumptions vs. interpretations before acting on it
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: One-directional enablement — 'gathers the raw, factual, and reliable data necessary for the frontal cortex to perform this logical, analytical work' — listening feeds data TO critical thinking rather than critical thinking strengthening the listening itself.
admission_edge.source_description: Critical-thinking turns active-listening into better judgment by using the gathered data to separate facts, assumptions, and interpretations.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When environmental signals suggest the current path needs revision but the team's existing beliefs about the strategy remain unchallenged by new evidence
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Direct blocking mechanism — 'The innate drive to seek out and interpret information that affirms existing beliefs prevents genuine adaptation' — specifically targets adaptation's core requirement of updating behavior based on new signals.
admission_edge.source_description: Confirmation-bias blocks adaptation when new signals are interpreted to defend the current path instead of changing it.
Adaptation conflicts with commitment-bias when prior commitments suppress necessary course-correction under new evidence.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When environmental conditions are changing and the system needs signal structures to detect when and how current behavior must be revised
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Described as 'the mechanism of successful adaptation' — understanding feedback loops and emergent interactions enables the smarter planning and decision-making that adaptation requires.
admission_edge.source_description: Feedback-loops gives adaptation the signal structure it needs to revise behavior under changing environmental conditions.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When cognitive shortcuts in the screening process may produce systematically biased assessments of counterparty quality or information signals
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Extremely generic — 'Mental models are used to combat biases, which are the tendency of the brain to take shortcuts' — barely specific enough to be useful for adverse-selection in particular.
admission_edge.source_description: Cognitive-biases undermine adverse-selection analysis by pushing the operator toward shortcut-driven judgment instead of objective hypothesis testing.
Adverse-selection conflicts with confirmation-bias when screeners overweight the signals that fit their prior beliefs about quality.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When the screening model needs to be tested for whether it is actually detecting hidden-information signals or just confirming prior quality assumptions
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Generic reflective capability — 'stepping outside one's current mental models to examine neutrally whether they are working' — supports but does not specifically strengthen adverse-selection analysis.
admission_edge.source_description: Critical-thinking supports adverse-selection by stepping outside the current frame and testing whether the chosen model is actually working.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When sprint hypotheses are pre-determined to confirm a mandated conclusion rather than genuinely testing the underlying assumptions
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Generic confirmation bias applied to the Agile context — 'hypothesis-driven sprints are used to confirm a mandated conclusion' — the mechanism is about misuse of Agile rather than a specific anti-Agile force.
admission_edge.source_description: Confirmation-bias turns agile-methodologies into ritualized hypothesis protection by using sprints to confirm a favored conclusion.
Agile-methodologies conflicts with optimization-theory when sprint-local velocity targets degrade end-to-end system performance.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When iterative delivery needs a test-everything discipline to convert sprint cycles into genuine validated learning rather than recycled assumptions
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: The canonical article describes hypothesis-driven problem solving as 'a core ally' — the disciplined test-everything approach that converts sprint cycles into genuine learning rather than opinion recycling.
admission_edge.source_description: Experimentation gives agile-methodologies the test-everything discipline needed to turn iteration into real learning instead of opinion recycling.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When new disconfirming evidence is available but the team's existing beliefs about the uncertainty type may prevent them from updating their assessment
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Directly targets AEUR's core function — 'prevents recognition of disconfirming evidence needed to reduce epistemic ignorance' — blocks the evidence updating that uncertainty reduction requires.
admission_edge.source_description: Confirmation-bias prevents aleatory-epistemic-uncertainty-recognition from updating ignorance honestly because disconfirming evidence never changes the uncertainty map.
Aleatory-epistemic-uncertainty-recognition conflicts with commitment-bias when teams persist with single-path plans despite unresolved unknowns.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When uncertainty estimates need to be grounded in population-level frequency data rather than subjective confidence about the specific case
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Indirect grounding tool — 'anchoring decisions in the outside view' — provides population-level reference data to discipline uncertainty estimates, but not described as the core mechanism of AEUR itself.
admission_edge.source_description: Base-rates helps aleatory-epistemic-uncertainty-recognition discipline the inside view with outside-view statistical grounding.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When the procedure being designed embeds untested assumptions about how the process should work rather than testing against actual edge cases
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Generic application — 'procedure design embeds assumptions' — about unexamined assumptions baked into procedure design, not a specific anti-algorithmic mechanism.
admission_edge.source_description: Confirmation-bias can get baked into the procedure when the algorithm is designed to confirm the designer's prior model rather than test it against hard cases.
Algorithmic-thinking conflicts with feedback-loops when static rule pipelines fail to update after signal drift.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When the algorithm needs explicit boundary rules for edge cases, valid input ranges, and coordination across specialized processing paths
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Operational supplement — 'explicit branching rules, bounded edge cases, and coordination' — provides the boundary parameters that algorithms need but is a tool-level rather than mechanism-level relationship.
admission_edge.source_description: Constraints help algorithmic-thinking define bounded edge cases, reliable handoffs, and the limits within which the procedure should operate.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When familiar analogies from past experience persist in guiding thinking even though the new context requires a genuinely different framing
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Related persistence mechanism — 'thinkers persist in using mental models that are unhelpful or misleading in a new context' — about stickiness of old analogies rather than a direct attack on analogical reasoning itself.
admission_edge.source_description: Einstellung-effect undermines analogies-and-metaphors by locking onto the first familiar comparison so firmly that the thinker never tests whether a different analogy would map the target domain more accurately.
Analogies-and-metaphors conflicts with abstraction when vivid analogy transfer distorts the structural boundaries of the target domain.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When the audience does not yet have a usable mental model for the new concept but does have working knowledge in a structurally similar domain
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Described as the structural mechanism — 'Analogies provide the pre-existing mental model (the scaffold) off which new material can be piggybacked and built upon incrementally' — direct enabling mechanism for how analogies support learning.
admission_edge.source_description: Scaffolding helps analogies-and-metaphors work by giving a staged bridge from what the audience already knows to what it needs to learn next.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When salient initial figures or anecdotes are displacing population-level frequency data from the estimate or decision
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Direct replacement mechanism — 'decision-making should be anchored instead to the outside view, focusing on general outcomes and external data' — provides the alternative reference point that displaces arbitrary anchors.
admission_edge.source_description: Base-rates counters anchoring by replacing the inside-view frame with an outside-view reference point grounded in broader outcomes.
Anchoring conflicts with critical-thinking when the first frame becomes sticky enough to block real belief revision.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When presenting new information and can connect it to existing schemas to reduce working memory burden and improve processing efficiency
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Explains the benefit mechanism — 'Strategic anchoring reduces cognitive load' by connecting new concepts to existing schemas — but describes what anchoring achieves rather than how CLT strengthens anchoring's effectiveness.
admission_edge.source_description: Cognitive-load-theory helps anchoring work well by using familiar schemas to reduce working-memory burden during early orientation.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When evidence of fragility or system weakness is being filtered out to support the belief that current structures are already robust enough
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Generic application — 'causes individuals to seek out information that validates current beliefs, leading to a closed' mindset — standard bias-vs-model relationship without antifragility-specific mechanism.
admission_edge.source_description: Confirmation-bias makes antifragility brittle because it resists learning from disorder that contradicts the current model.
Antifragility conflicts with anchoring when planners underestimate cascade failure probability by anchoring on low individual-component failure rates.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When building antifragile capacity requires systematic testing of multiple approaches rather than relying on predicted outcomes from a single path
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Core operational discipline — 'adopt a portfolio of experiments approach, test every single possibility and systematically compare outcomes' — the mechanism by which antifragile capacity is deliberately built.
admission_edge.source_description: Experimentation gives antifragility a practical route to benefit from variation through many bounded tests rather than one brittle bet.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When associative links are being selectively activated to reinforce a pre-existing narrative rather than tested against disconfirming evidence
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Standard bias application — 'associative links are selectively activated to reinforce a pre-existing narrative' — real but generic mechanism without association-specific language.
admission_edge.source_description: Confirmation-bias makes association dangerous when it reinforces the first preferred pattern instead of testing alternatives.
Association conflicts with first-principles-thinking when familiar pattern-matching substitutes for decomposition of novel causal structure.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When connecting new concepts to existing knowledge structures requires the schema and mental-bucket mechanisms that analogical thinking provides
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Core structural mechanism — association works through schemas and mental buckets that analogies provide. The canonical describes association as 'the glue of the latticework' and analogies as the schema-building tools that enable it.
admission_edge.source_description: Analogies-and-metaphors strengthens association by turning new patterns into fast, recognizable mental buckets without long explanation.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When audit findings are being interpreted to confirm the desired conclusion about system health rather than objectively assessing the evidence trail
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Generic bias application — 'The tendency to process information to get a conclusion we want' — standard bias-vs-model relationship without auditability-specific mechanism.
admission_edge.source_description: Confirmation-bias corrupts auditability-traceability when the trail is built to justify a wanted answer instead of to expose how the judgment really formed.
Auditability-traceability conflicts with optionality when documentation overhead locks teams into a recorded path and discourages late-stage pivots.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When explicit workplanning with defined data sources and end products needs to create a definitive, step-by-step audit trail for downstream accountability
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Operational tool — 'Explicit Workplanning... creates the definitive audit trail' — provides the structural framework for traceability but is a tool-level complement rather than a core mechanism.
admission_edge.source_description: Constraints help auditability-traceability stay actionable by making boundaries, assumptions, and operating limits explicit inside the trail.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When commitment to one's authentic position drifts into motivated reasoning that processes information to reach a desired conclusion rather than facing radical truth
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Direct opposition — 'Authenticity requires facing radical truth, which conflicts with the brain's tendency to process information to reach a desired conclusion' — motivated reasoning is the core psychological threat to authentic thinking.
admission_edge.source_description: Confirmation-bias undermines authenticity when people defend a preferred self-story instead of facing uncomfortable truth.
Authority-bias conflicts with first-principles-thinking when inherited expert doctrine blocks ground-up decomposition.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When authentic interaction requires explicitly stating what each party wants and expects rather than operating through implicit assumptions or politeness norms
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Operational tool — 'asking directly, Here is what I want from you. What do you want from me?' — provides the explicit communication structure for authentic interaction but is a practice rather than a constitutive mechanism.
admission_edge.source_description: Boundaries helps authenticity turn candor into usable commitments instead of performative oversharing.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When the authority's recommendation needs to be evaluated on its evidential merit rather than accepted on the basis of status, credentials, or social pressure
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Described as demanding 'the ability to evaluate evidence, to notice bias as it kicks into gear' — specific, active counter-mechanism that directly opposes uncritical deference.
admission_edge.source_description: Critical thinking opposes authority bias by demanding evidence evaluation and active skepticism instead of automatic deference.
Authority-bias conflicts with confirmation-bias when deference to the expert selectively amplifies confirming evidence.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When the authority figure's initial framing fixes attention on their perspective before the decision-maker has independently considered alternative reference points
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Conditional amplifier — 'The selection of a specific expert or framework can serve as a potent anchor' — the authority's initial frame fixes attention, but the language is conditional ('can serve as').
admission_edge.source_description: Anchoring amplifies authority bias by fixing attention on the authority's frame before alternatives are considered.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When deep domain expertise makes the expert dismiss population-level evidence that contradicts their established pattern recognition from prior cases
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Secondary mechanism through expertise — 'Experts who have deep mastery may suffer from cognitive entrenchment' — causes dismissal of base-rate data that contradicts established expert patterns.
admission_edge.source_description: Einstellung-effect (cognitive entrenchment) causes experts to dismiss base-rate data that contradicts their specialized mental models — the fixation on domain-specific frameworks blocks the reference-class correction that base rates provide.
Base-rates conflicts with confirmation-bias when prior beliefs override inconvenient outside-view frequencies.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When base-rate priors need to be validated against repeatable, objective historical evidence rather than accepted as intuitively reasonable estimates
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Specific calibration mechanism — 'demands that beliefs be calibrated based on objective, repeatable evidence (historical frequency)' — the discipline that makes base-rate estimates evidence-based rather than intuitive.
admission_edge.source_description: The scientific method supports base rates by forcing beliefs to be calibrated against repeatable historical evidence instead of vivid specifics.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When the first data point or frame encountered is being treated as the baseline without independent verification that it represents the actual starting conditions
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Directly corrupts the model's core function — 'the Baseline acts as an anchor' — when the first data point encountered becomes the baseline without independent verification, the entire subsequent analysis is built on a biased foundation.
admission_edge.source_description: Anchoring undermines baseline-establishment by letting the first data point or frame encountered become the de facto baseline, preventing the team from defining a genuinely representative starting condition.
Baseline-establishment conflicts with confirmation-bias when evidence is filtered to preserve the existing baseline instead of honestly challenging whether it still reflects reality.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When the baseline needs to be preserved as a traceable reference point for future comparison rather than being lost or distorted as the project evolves
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Recording complement — 'Successful outcomes are predicated on defining a clear, accurate starting point against which all subsequent analysis and measurement can be compared' — preserves the baseline as a durable reference.
admission_edge.source_description: Auditability-traceability gives baseline-establishment a durable record of what the starting condition actually was, so later change claims can be checked.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When the first attractive walk-away option encountered anchors the negotiator and prevents genuine exploration of potentially superior alternatives
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Directly blocks BATNA exploration — 'If the first available alternative is attractive, anchoring prevents exploring truly superior options' — narrows the search space prematurely.
admission_edge.source_description: Anchoring undermines BATNA by making the first attractive option feel like the only serious alternative worth considering.
Batna conflicts with commitment-bias when sunk negotiation posture blocks rational walk-away updates.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When the team needs a concrete, manageable starting point for building negotiation alternatives rather than facing an overwhelming landscape of options
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Incremental building mechanism — 'Choosing a manageable alternative or starting point allows for the gradual, incremental building of a complex structure' — supports BATNA development but is a tool-level relationship.
admission_edge.source_description: Scaffolding is an ally to BATNA because identifying a clear, manageable walk-away alternative creates an incremental framework for building negotiation competence — starting from the grounded fallback option and progressively constructing more sophisticated positioning.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When the initial prior estimate is keeping disproportionate weight despite accumulating evidence that should have shifted the posterior substantially
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Specific Bayesian failure mode — 'too much focus is placed on a single, often initial, piece of information' — the prior absorbs disproportionate weight and subsequent evidence fails to shift the posterior adequately.
admission_edge.source_description: Anchoring distorts bayesian reasoning when the initial prior keeps too much weight after contradictory evidence arrives.
Bayesian conflicts with confirmation-bias when posterior updates are blocked by selective evidence acceptance.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When Bayesian analysis needs an objective outside-view prior grounded in population-level frequencies before incorporating case-specific evidence
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Constitutive — 'anchor initial estimates to reference classes' — base rates ARE the prior probability that Bayesian reasoning starts from. Without a principled prior, the entire updating process is ungrounded.
admission_edge.source_description: Base-rates stabilizes bayesian reasoning by supplying the outside-view prior before case-specific evidence is layered in.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When the inability to see one's own biases provides the psychological foundation for selectively seeking confirming evidence without any awareness of doing so
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Constitutive enabling — 'The BBS provides the foundation for confirmation bias' — bias-blind-spot is what makes confirmation bias invisible to the person exhibiting it, a foundational rather than merely synergistic relationship.
admission_edge.source_description: Confirmation-bias is reinforced by bias-blind-spot when self-unaware reasoning seeks support for existing conclusions while overlooking disconfirming information.
Black-swan-events conflicts with anchoring when people anchor on low component failure rates and underestimate whole-system fragility.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When the default critical stance is directed outward at others' reasoning and needs to be deliberately turned inward to examine one's own susceptibility to bias
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Directional shift — 'seek objective reality outside of our subjective perception' — supports BBS correction by turning analytical scrutiny inward, but is a general capability rather than a BBS-specific mechanism.
admission_edge.source_description: Critical-thinking supports bias-blind-spot correction by shifting the target of scrutiny from other people's stories to the evidence behind your own.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When past experience with normal outcomes creates an anchor that prevents proper estimation of rare but catastrophic event probabilities
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Specific mechanism targeting tail-risk estimation — 'causes people to underestimate the overall failure rate' — past experience with normal outcomes creates an anchor that blinds to extreme-event probabilities.
admission_edge.source_description: Anchoring works against black-swan caution when it causes people to underestimate the overall failure probability of fragile complex systems.

Black-swan-events conflicts with hindsight-bias when retrospective narratives make rare, genuinely unpredictable events appear to have been foreseeable, corrupting organizational learning about tail-risk exposure.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When robust execution discipline is needed to close the gap between intellectual awareness of tail risks and consistent organizational preparedness routines
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Generic operational tool — 'structured around checklists and disciplined execution frameworks' — supports consistent preparedness practices but without black-swan-specific mechanism. Thin source evidence.
admission_edge.source_description: Checklists support black-swan readiness when robust execution discipline is needed to close the gap between strategy and the unexpected obstacle.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When the analytical evaluation stage requires impartial assessment but existing beliefs distort the analysis to confirm expected conclusions rather than discovering genuine insights
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Targets a specific level — 'skews the impartiality required for Analyze and compromises' evaluation — undermines mid-level taxonomy operations but not the entire cognitive progression model.
admission_edge.source_description: Confirmation-bias undermines blooms-taxonomy by distorting the impartial analysis and evaluation needed before strong judgment or synthesis can be trusted.
Blooms-taxonomy conflicts with decomposition when rigid level-by-level progression prevents parallel exploration of higher-order insights that emerge before lower levels are complete.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When verifying that foundational understanding and analysis levels are solid before the learner advances to synthesis, evaluation, and creation
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Described as 'a practical method to test the integrity of the lower cognitive levels' — directly serves the taxonomy's progression discipline by exposing knowledge gaps before advancement.
admission_edge.source_description: Feynman-technique helps blooms-taxonomy test whether lower stages are solid enough before the learner attempts more complex analytical or evaluative work.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When fast intuitive processing is producing constraint diagnoses based on pattern-matching shortcuts rather than the disciplined serial analysis that bottleneck identification requires
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Directly opposes the analysis mode — 'the disciplined, slow, and serial nature of processing at the bottleneck stands in contrast to Type 1 thinking, which is fast, intuitive, and relies on mental shortcuts' — heuristic processing actively misidentifies constraints.
admission_edge.source_description: System-1's fast, intuitive, shortcut-driven processing directly opposes bottleneck thinking — bottleneck analysis requires the disciplined, slow, serial processing of System 2, while System 1's heuristics produce the pattern-jumping that misidentifies constraints and bypasses the real limit.
Bottlenecks conflicts with confirmation-bias when teams protect the chosen constraint diagnosis instead of testing alternate system limiters.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When bottleneck identification requires understanding that working memory limits are the primary cognitive constraint driving throughput failures in learning or decision-making
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Described as 'a direct ally' where 'the central finding of CLT—that working memory is limited—is the primary cognitive bottleneck the theory seeks to manage' — CLT defines the foundational constraint that bottleneck analysis targets.
admission_edge.source_description: Cognitive Load Theory is a direct ally because bottlenecks often show up as working-memory limits that need chunking and scaffolding.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When scope boundaries are being drawn by a familiar theoretical framework rather than derived from the actual problem structure and available evidence
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Directly corrupts boundary placement — described as 'a direct challenge to the wise use of boundaries' where a familiar model dictates scope instead of the real objective and evidence landscape.
admission_edge.source_description: Theory-induced-blindness undermines boundaries when a familiar frame dictates the scope instead of the real objective and evidence landscape.
Boundaries conflicts with optionality when prematurely fixed boundaries close off adjacent opportunities that emerge only through exploratory scope expansion.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When scope boundaries need to be sized to respect working memory limits rather than set by arbitrary project convention or stakeholder ambition
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Directly informs the boundary mechanism — 'the boundary of limited working memory informs the effective strategy of Scaffolding' — CLT provides the empirical justification for why boundaries must respect cognitive capacity.
admission_edge.source_description: Cognitive-load-theory gives boundaries a concrete limit condition by showing why genuinely manageable chunks matter for real comprehension and execution.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When the presence or status of a senior participant is causing team members to self-censor their ideas or defer to the authority's framing rather than generating independently
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Directly suppresses the core function — 'Team members suppress their ideas due to pressure, loyalty, or the presence of a senior person' — kills divergent generation by collapsing the group's search space to the authority's frame.
admission_edge.source_description: Authority-bias undermines brainstorming by causing team members to suppress their own ideas and defer to the senior person's framing, collapsing the divergent space the session needs.
Brainstorming conflicts with anchoring when the first idea introduced becomes the reference point that constrains the rest of the session.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When brainstorming sessions need to produce genuinely novel alternatives rather than variations on the same underlying idea or the group's existing direction
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Essential reframing mechanism — turns raw idea volume into 'genuinely reframed alternatives rather than more of the same answer' — differentiates productive brainstorming from mere repetition by providing the divergent quality that volume alone cannot.
admission_edge.source_description: Lateral-thinking strengthens brainstorming by turning raw idea volume into genuinely reframed alternatives rather than more of the same answer.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When the initial problem framing or analytical structure adopted in the Branch phase is constraining how later evidence is interpreted rather than being revised by it
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Framework-fixation risk — 'apply familiar frameworks routinely and unquestioningly' — the first analytical frame hardens before branch evidence can challenge it, but the language is conditional rather than describing a direct blocking mechanism.
admission_edge.source_description: Anchoring weakens branch-solve-merge when the first frame or branch structure hardens too early and later evidence gets forced back into it.
Branch-solve-merge conflicts with commitment-bias when teams continue one merge path despite branch evidence divergence.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When the Branch phase needs a specific methodology for dividing the problem into non-overlapping, workable sub-problems
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Practical entry tool — 'turning a large problem into logical pieces that can actually be worked' — provides the Branch phase's analytical cut but is a tool applied within BSM rather than the framework itself.
admission_edge.source_description: Decomposition gives branch-solve-merge its practical entry point by turning a large problem into logical pieces that can actually be worked.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When preference for parsimonious explanations is suppressing investigation of interconnected causal chains in systems where nonlinear dynamics may amplify small initial differences
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Direct conceptual opposition — 'clashes directly with the premise of the Butterfly Effect' — preference for the simplest explanation suppresses attention to the intertwined causal chains that matter in nonlinear systems.
admission_edge.source_description: Occams-razor can suppress butterfly-effect when preference for simple explanations hides the intertwined causal chains that matter in nonlinear systems.
Butterfly-effect conflicts with representativeness-heuristic when local similarity hides nonlinear cascade risk.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When initial-condition analysis needs to extend beyond immediate first-order effects to trace the full cascade of downstream consequences across the system
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Described as compelled by the model — 'The model compels us to engage in second-order thinking and visualize the entire chain of consequences' — required cognitive mode for butterfly-effect analysis, not merely complementary.
admission_edge.source_description: Second-order-thinking makes butterfly-effect actionable by forcing attention onto downstream consequences instead of only immediate outcomes.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When risk estimates are anchored to the most likely (mean) scenario rather than properly weighting the full distribution including tail risks and conjunctive failure probabilities
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Directly corrupts risk calculation — 'focusing too heavily on the mean outcome' and 'unwarranted optimism about success' — overweights upside scenarios and underestimates real downside exposure, making the 'calculated' part of risk-taking illusory.
admission_edge.source_description: Optimism-bias-and-planning-fallacy undermines calculated-risk-taking by overweighting upside scenarios and underestimating the real downside exposure.
Calculated-risk-taking conflicts with black-swan-events when systematic risk estimation creates false precision around outcomes whose probability distributions have fat tails.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When uncertain risk paths need to be laid out as an explicit branching structure with probability-weighted payoffs to enable systematic comparison of alternatives
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Structural comparison tool — 'concrete branching structure for comparing uncertain paths and explicit payoffs' — provides the analytical scaffolding for risk comparison but is a tool applied within the risk framework.
admission_edge.source_description: Decision-trees gives calculated-risk-taking a concrete branching structure for comparing uncertain paths and explicit payoffs.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When existing category assignments are being defended based on political comfort or familiarity rather than subjected to the objective evidence-based review that accurate categorization requires
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Directly blocks objective review — 'predisposition to defend existing beliefs or mental models' — fights against the evidence-based reassessment that category decisions require, causing categories to be defended for comfort rather than accuracy.
admission_edge.source_description: Confirmation-bias distorts category-decisions when the bucket is defended for political comfort instead of evidence.
Category-decisions conflicts with first-principles-thinking when inherited buckets replace decomposition of underlying mechanisms.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When category boundaries need to be validated by explicitly mapping the branching logic that separates cases and their consequences before the categorization rule is locked in
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Practical structuring tool — 'tools used to cleave a problem into insightful parts' — provides the analytical cut for category separation but operates as one framework among several rather than being constitutive of the categorization process.
admission_edge.source_description: Decision-trees helps category-decisions separate cases and consequences before the rule is locked in.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When the initial causal attribution has hardened into a defended narrative and subsequent evidence is being selectively interpreted to confirm it rather than genuinely test alternatives
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Powerful locking mechanism — 'A powerful bias where people process information to get a conclusion they want rather than what is true' — locks premature attribution into a defended causal story by selectively filtering subsequent evidence.
admission_edge.source_description: Confirmation-bias undermines causal-attribution-resistance by locking onto the first plausible culprit and selectively reading later evidence through that story.
Causal-attribution-resistance conflicts with incentive-blind diagnosis when a moralized blame story hides the structural payoffs producing the behavior.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When skepticism needs to be directed specifically at the most narratively satisfying causal explanation rather than accepting it because it feels complete and emotionally resolving
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Described as foundational — canonical states 'CAR is an advanced form of critical thinking' involving 'the ability to question one's own biases, evaluate evidence, and willingly consider opposing perspectives' — the broader cognitive capacity of which CAR is a specialized application.
admission_edge.source_description: Critical-thinking strengthens causal-attribution-resistance by forcing skepticism toward the most narratively satisfying explanation.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When an early intermediate conclusion in the reasoning chain is being accepted and subsequent steps are being constructed to support it rather than genuinely testing it
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Conditional corruption — 'the tendency to jump to conclusions before the chain is tested' — the first plausible intermediate answer can anchor subsequent steps, but the mechanism is conditional rather than a direct blocking force.
admission_edge.source_description: Anchoring can corrupt chain-of-thought when the first plausible answer determines the later steps instead of being tested by them.
Chain-of-thought conflicts with lateral-thinking when sequential step-by-step decomposition suppresses non-linear leaps that would reach a better solution faster.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When the problem needs to be broken into smaller, logically connected steps before sequential reasoning can meaningfully progress through the chain
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Practical structuring tool — 'decomposition of a complex problem into a sequence of smaller, logically connected steps' — provides the analytical cut that gives CoT its step-by-step character but is a tool applied within CoT rather than the reasoning mode itself.
admission_edge.source_description: Decomposition strengthens chain-of-thought by forcing the problem into smaller linked units before any final answer is trusted.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When the verification process is unconsciously confirming prior steps and preferred conclusions rather than genuinely testing each link for disconfirmation
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Directly opposes the verification function — 'CoV demands radical open-mindedness and intellectual humility, forcing the thinker to identify and reconcile disconfirming evidence' — confirmation bias converts verification into validation of the preferred story.
admission_edge.source_description: Confirmation-bias pressures chain-of-verification to validate the preferred story rather than reconcile disconfirming evidence link by link.
Chain-of-verification conflicts with optionality when exhaustive step-by-step verification delays action past the window where cheap reversible experiments would yield more learning.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When each link in the verification chain needs genuine evaluative scrutiny of evidence quality and logical validity rather than ceremonial confirmation of prior steps
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Core questioning discipline — 'Critical thinking involves systematically evaluating evidence' and 'the goal of CoV is to cultivate a sound path to conclusions' — provides the evaluative rigor that makes each verification step genuinely probative.
admission_edge.source_description: Critical-thinking gives chain-of-verification the questioning discipline that checks whether each premise deserves to stay in the argument.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When the discipline of avoiding false precision is being used to dismiss necessary engagement with complex system dynamics rather than simply ensuring that outputs acknowledge their inherent uncertainty
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Guardrail tension — 'the guardrail that chaos-theory calls for, and chaotic conditions make fake precision especially dangerous' — the discipline of avoiding false precision can conflict with chaos-theory when it becomes an excuse not to engage with the complex modeling that chaotic systems require.
admission_edge.source_description: False-precision-avoidance is the guardrail that chaos-theory calls for, and chaotic conditions make fake precision especially dangerous.

Chaos-theory conflicts with algorithmic-thinking when algorithmic thinking emphasizes predictability and structured problem-solving, contrasting with chaos theory's focus on unpredictability and non-linearity.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When chaos-theory analysis needs a concrete mechanism for reasoning about how small perturbations in initial conditions can propagate into radically different system outcomes
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Near-identity — 'The literal term Butterfly Effect is most closely associated with Chaos Theory and sensitive dependence on initial conditions' — butterfly-effect IS the concrete mechanism through which chaos theory's core principle of sensitive dependence becomes observable and actionable.
admission_edge.source_description: Butterfly-effect gives chaos-theory a concrete way to reason about sensitive dependence and nonlinear propagation through a system.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When a previously successful checklist is being applied to a genuinely novel problem and the familiar steps are forcing reality into a framework whose assumptions no longer hold
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Specific misapplication threat — 'applying a generic checklist to a genuinely novel problem risks disastrously wrong solutions' — cognitive entrenchment causes practitioners to reach for a familiar checklist when the situation demands a different framework entirely.
admission_edge.source_description: Einstellung-effect undermines checklists by causing practitioners to apply a previously successful checklist to a genuinely novel problem, forcing reality into familiar steps rather than testing whether the checklist's assumptions still hold.
Checklists conflicts with flow when procedural interruption for checklist compliance breaks the concentrated absorption that creative tasks require.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When procedural complexity exceeds working memory capacity and explicit externalization into checklist steps is needed to prevent cognitive overload errors
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Explains why checklists work — 'The model is a countermeasure to cognitive overload' — CLT provides the scientific basis for externalizing procedural burden, making checklists not just practical but cognitively justified.
admission_edge.source_description: Cognitive-load-theory explains why checklists work: they move procedural burden off limited working memory and into explicit steps.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When borrowing expertise from an authority figure or credential and the alignment with one's own proven domain boundaries has not been explicitly tested
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Directly pulls judgment outside the earned perimeter — external expert status gets accepted without testing whether it falls within proven domain boundaries.
admission_edge.source_description: Authority-bias can pull judgment outside the earned perimeter by making borrowed expertise feel sufficient.
Circle-of-competence conflicts with commitment-bias when teams keep operating outside capability limits to protect prior decisions.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When defining the precise boundary between what is actually understood versus what is assumed or inherited without verification
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Described as 'a direct tool for defining the perimeter' — directly serves CoC's core function of boundary definition through a specific, actionable method.
admission_edge.source_description: The Feynman technique helps circle-of-competence expose the perimeter by revealing what cannot yet be explained simply.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When the team is classifying difficult-but-influenceable factors as uncontrollable without testing whether influence could actually be increased through effort, changed incentives, or new information
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Directly corrupts the model's core function — 'labeling difficult-but-influenceable factors as outside control too early, which can become avoidance disguised as realism' — turns the control classification exercise into a tool for avoiding difficult action.
admission_edge.source_description: Status-quo-bias undermines circle-of-control by causing teams to classify difficult-but-influenceable factors as 'outside control' without testing whether influence could actually be increased, turning the model into avoidance disguised as realism.
Circle-of-control conflicts with game-theory-payoffs when opponents can shift what is influenceable faster than the current control map assumes.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When items classified as uncontrollable need to be decomposed into underlying assumptions to test whether some component is actually within the team's influence
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Complement — 'works well with First Principles Thinking, where constraints are decomposed into controllable assumptions and testable actions' — useful pairing but 'works well with' indicates moderate complement rather than deep dependency.
admission_edge.source_description: First-principles-thinking helps circle-of-control decompose constraints into assumptions and testable actions instead of treating the whole situation as one helpless block.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When a fluent, confident claim from an authority figure is being accepted without the bias-checking scrutiny that cognitive-biases awareness demands
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Amplification mechanism — 'making fluent confident claims feel credible before they are tested' — compounds cognitive biases by causing untested acceptance of authoritative-sounding assertions, though the canonical names this indirectly through System 1 takeover.
admission_edge.source_description: Authority-bias compounds cognitive-biases by making fluent confident claims feel credible before they are tested.
Cognitive-biases conflicts with bias-blind-spot when cataloguing biases in others creates the illusion of personal immunity to the same distortions.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When awareness of cognitive biases needs to be converted into active self-reflection that questions assumptions, evaluates evidence quality, and identifies where personal experience is distorting judgment
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Described as 'essential for recognizing and overcoming biases' — canonical states 'Metacognition & Critical Thinking is essential' — the core cognitive capacity that makes bias awareness actionable rather than merely intellectual.
admission_edge.source_description: Critical-thinking strengthens cognitive-biases by turning bias awareness into active questioning of assumptions, evidence, and self-deception.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When honest evaluation of conflicting evidence is being converted into motivated advocacy for the pre-committed position by the discomfort of inconsistency
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Directly opposed cognitive operation — 'requires engaging honestly with evidence that conflicts with current beliefs — exactly what dissonance-motivated reasoning prevents' — dissonance converts critical scrutiny into motivated advocacy.
admission_edge.source_description: Critical thinking requires engaging honestly with evidence that conflicts with current beliefs — exactly the cognitive operation that dissonance-motivated reasoning is designed to prevent.

Cognitive-dissonance conflicts with intellectual-humility when the motivated drive to eliminate belief inconsistency converts contrary evidence into a threat to be defended against rather than information to be genuinely updated on.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When the information-gathering process has quietly shifted to finding evidence that supports a committed position, and this selective filtering is functioning as dissonance reduction rather than genuine inquiry
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Primary resolution tool — 'one of cognitive dissonance's primary resolution tools: seeking confirming evidence reduces the dissonance that would arise if contradictory evidence were weighted honestly' — the mechanism through which dissonance operates on the evidence stream.
admission_edge.source_description: Confirmation bias is one of cognitive dissonance's primary resolution tools — seeking out confirming evidence and minimizing disconfirming evidence reduces the dissonance that would arise if contradictory evidence were weighted honestly.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When existing capability narratives are being defended rather than honestly tested, causing the assessment to overweight evidence of competence and overlook data that would reveal gaps
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Directly opposes gap discovery — canonical states 'The drive to interpret information to confirm existing beliefs actively ignores, dismisses, or overlooks data that would expose a gap in understanding' — makes gaps invisible by overweighting favorable capability narratives.
admission_edge.source_description: Confirmation-bias blocks cognitive-gaps-assessment when already-favored capability stories receive more weight than reality deserves.
Cognitive-gaps-assessment conflicts with authority-bias when rank substitutes for objective competency evidence.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When understanding needs to be stress-tested by attempting simple explanation, and failure points in the explanation directly reveal the cognitive gaps that need to be addressed
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Direct gap-surfacing mechanism — canonical describes it as 'explicitly forcing the identification of one's mental blind spots' — plain-language explanation reveals exactly where understanding collapses, which IS cognitive gap assessment in action.
admission_edge.source_description: Feynman-technique strengthens cognitive-gaps-assessment by exposing where understanding collapses under plain-language explanation.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When expert communication is adding unnecessary complexity that increases the audience's cognitive load because the expert has forgotten what it is like not to know the material
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Directly increases the load CLT manages — 'The innate tendency of experts to communicate complexity, directly increasing the novice's cognitive load' — experts communicate at their own abstraction level, imposing unnecessary extrinsic load.
admission_edge.source_description: Curse-of-knowledge undermines cognitive-load-theory by causing experts to communicate at their own level of abstraction, directly increasing the novice's cognitive load instead of reducing it.
Cognitive-load-theory conflicts with first-principles-thinking when deep decomposition overloads working memory before the core abstraction is stable.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When problem complexity is exceeding working memory capacity and decomposition into logical branches is needed to limit the number of variables that must be held simultaneously
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Directly serves CLT's core mechanism — 'Logic trees make it easy to see the structure of the problem. This limits the number of variables the working memory must consider simultaneously' — decomposition IS the structural technique that reduces working memory demand.
admission_edge.source_description: Decomposition helps cognitive-load-theory break a problem into logical pieces that working memory can actually manage.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When the team is defending a single-cause explanation for an outcome rather than investigating whether multiple interacting factors are jointly responsible
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Blocks multi-factor analysis — 'motivated reasoning prevents honest adaptation to reality' — causes teams to defend a single-cause explanation rather than following the interacting drivers that combinatorial analysis would reveal.
admission_edge.source_description: Confirmation-bias blocks combinatorial-effects when teams defend a favorite single-cause story instead of following the interacting drivers.
Combinatorial-effects conflicts with occams-razor when combinatorial explanations are preferred over simpler models that predict equally well with fewer interacting terms.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When the immediate combinatorial interaction needs to be traced forward to understand downstream cascade effects that emerge from the multi-factor alignment
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Downstream tracking complement — 'seeing the relatedness and the effects from the relatedness' — extends combinatorial analysis to cascade effects but is a complement rather than constitutive of the multi-factor interaction itself.
admission_edge.source_description: Second-order-thinking helps combinatorial-effects track the downstream dominoes created when several forces compound at once.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When the drive for consistency with a prior commitment is biasing evidence evaluation to confirm the original decision rather than genuinely testing it against new information
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Specific amplification — 'Consistency amplifies confirmation bias by driving individuals to seek information that confirms their existing commitment' — the commitment acts as a filter that biases all subsequent evidence gathering.
admission_edge.source_description: Confirmation bias compounds commitment bias by making the operator search for evidence that justifies the existing commitment.
Commitment-bias conflicts with optionality when the need to appear consistent forecloses reversible alternatives that would preserve future flexibility.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When a prior commitment is generating psychological discomfort (dissonance) that drives the individual to rationalize and adjust beliefs to match the committed position rather than update honestly
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Constitutive engine — 'Commitment is the fuel for cognitive dissonance' — cognitive dissonance is the psychological mechanism that PRODUCES commitment bias; the discomfort of inconsistency drives the rationalizing behavior.
admission_edge.source_description: Cognitive dissonance is the psychological engine that powers commitment bias -- the discomfort of holding 'I committed to X' alongside contrary evidence generates the motivated drive to maintain the committed position rather than update honestly.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When evidence suggests the current task allocation is suboptimal but the team is defending the existing role map based on familiarity or politics rather than comparative efficiency
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Blocks reallocation — 'preventing them from detecting contradictory information' — causes teams to defend existing role allocations even when evidence shows the current distribution is suboptimal.
admission_edge.source_description: Confirmation-bias makes comparative-advantage defend an existing role map even after the evidence says the allocation is wrong.
Comparative-advantage conflicts with commitment-bias when sunk ownership prevents reallocating tasks by marginal efficiency.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When task or resource allocation needs to account for what is being sacrificed elsewhere by keeping work with its current owner rather than reallocating by relative efficiency
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Foundational concept — opportunity cost IS what makes comparative advantage calculable; without understanding what is lost when work stays with the wrong owner, the allocation decision has no basis.
admission_edge.source_description: Opportunity-cost sharpens comparative-advantage by showing what is lost when work stays with the wrong owner.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When the pursuit of optionality through constant branching and pivoting is preventing the stable learning loops that the adaptive system needs to mature and self-correct
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Conditional conflict — 'option churn undermines stable learning loops needed for system adaptation' — constant branching prevents the stability that CAS needs for its feedback loops to mature.
admission_edge.source_description: Optionality can clash with complex-adaptive-systems when constant branching churn prevents stable learning loops from forming.
Comparative-political-systems-analysis conflicts with first-principles-thinking when regime-specific precedent crowds out reconstruction from base institutional assumptions.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When comparing political systems requires understanding how different institutional rules create different incentive structures and strategic responses among political actors
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Actor modeling tool — 'Game theory thinking is the right tool to use in difficult competitive and adversarial settings' — clarifies how different actors respond under different system rules, but operates as one analytical tool within CPSA.
admission_edge.source_description: Game-theory-payoffs supports comparative-political-systems-analysis by clarifying how different actors respond under different system rules and incentives.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When the pursuit of optionality through constant branching and pivoting is preventing the stable learning loops that the adaptive system needs to mature and self-correct
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Conditional conflict — 'option churn undermines stable learning loops needed for system adaptation' — constant branching prevents the stability that CAS needs for its feedback loops to mature.
admission_edge.source_description: Optionality can clash with complex-adaptive-systems when constant branching churn prevents stable learning loops from forming.
Complexity-bias-resistance conflicts with combinatorial-effects when resistance to complexity dismisses genuine multi-factor interactions as unnecessary elaboration.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When the system's adaptive behavior depends on outputs being routed back as inputs and the analysis needs to trace how these feedback cycles shape learning and self-organization
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Core operational mechanism — 'Systems are feedback-dominated, meaning outputs are continually routed back as inputs' — feedback loops ARE the mechanism through which CAS adapts and self-organizes.
admission_edge.source_description: Feedback-loops make complex-adaptive-systems operational by showing how outputs return as inputs and reshape later behavior.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When the initial problem framing is preventing recognition that a simpler and more accurate explanatory cut exists because attention is anchored to the first framework encountered
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Frame-fixation — 'Focusing too heavily on the first piece of information or the initial problem framing prevents the recognition of a simpler, better solution' — locks analysis into the first frame rather than seeking the simplest accurate cut.
admission_edge.source_description: Anchoring undermines complexity-bias-resistance by locking problem framing onto the first piece of information encountered, preventing recognition of a simpler and more accurate explanatory cut.
Complexity-bias-resistance conflicts with combinatorial-effects when resistance to complexity dismisses genuine multi-factor interactions as unnecessary elaboration.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When a simplified model needs to be tested to verify that the reduction preserved the governing causal logic rather than producing a superficially clean but inaccurate story
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Validation discipline — 'Ensuring decisions and communications are grounded in essential clarity' — tests whether simplification preserves the real logic rather than producing a neat but misleading reduction.
admission_edge.source_description: Critical-thinking helps complexity-bias-resistance test whether a reduction preserves the real logic of the case instead of just sounding neat.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When an initial confidence estimate is resisting adjustment despite accumulating evidence because the original anchor is exerting disproportionate pull on subsequent estimates
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Miscalibration vector — 'Unwarranted Optimism / Planning Fallacy / Anchoring' — initial estimates create a reference point that prevents proper recalibration as new evidence arrives.
admission_edge.source_description: Anchoring can freeze confidence-calibration around an early estimate so later evidence fails to widen or narrow the range appropriately.
Compounding conflicts with margin-of-safety when projecting compound growth rates forward without accounting for the fragility of the base that sustains them.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When early-stage effort has not yet reached the threshold where compound acceleration begins and understanding the distance to critical mass is needed to maintain patience and investment
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Threshold concept — 'the threshold needed before rapid growth and compounding can occur. Once critical mass is reached, the positive effects begin to accelerate and compound' — critical mass defines when compounding shifts from linear to exponential.
admission_edge.source_description: Critical-mass helps compounding distinguish between early accumulation and the threshold where gains start accelerating.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When an initial confidence estimate is resisting adjustment despite accumulating evidence because the original anchor is exerting disproportionate pull on subsequent estimates
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Miscalibration vector — 'Unwarranted Optimism / Planning Fallacy / Anchoring' — initial estimates create a reference point that prevents proper recalibration as new evidence arrives.
admission_edge.source_description: Anchoring can freeze confidence-calibration around an early estimate so later evidence fails to widen or narrow the range appropriately.
Confidence-calibration conflicts with authority-bias when well-calibrated confidence in one domain is transferred uncritically to domains where the calibrator lacks expertise.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When personal confidence needs to be anchored to population-level frequencies so that the inside view is calibrated against what is generally true rather than what feels true from personal experience
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Calibration anchor — 'anchors the inside view to the outside view' and 'accuracy lives at the intersection of these two views' — base rates provide the external reality check that prevents calibration from drifting into subjective comfort.
admission_edge.source_description: Base-rates anchor confidence-calibration to the outside view so conviction is disciplined by what tends to happen in the world.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When team decision-making needs a formal structure to ensure contradictory evidence receives equal deliberation weight
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Institutionalizes challenge by requiring every thesis to meet its antithesis before synthesis — a structured process-level counter that directly opposes one-sided evidence filtering.
admission_edge.source_description: Dialectical reasoning opposes confirmation bias by institutionalizing challenge and antithesis before synthesis.
Confirmation-bias conflicts with critical-thinking when critical thinking insists on weighing all evidence instead of only confirming material.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When new information conflicts with prior decisions, self-image, or publicly stated positions, creating psychological pressure to filter selectively
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Direct causal driver — cognitive dissonance creates the psychological discomfort that confirmation bias 'serves as the protective mechanism' against, making it the underlying need the bias fulfills.
admission_edge.source_description: Cognitive-dissonance powers confirmation bias by making inconsistent information psychologically painful — the discomfort of conflicting beliefs drives the bias to selectively filter incoming evidence so that new information aligns with previous decisions or self-image.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When the team is selectively gathering evidence that supports the conjunctive plan's viability while overlooking data points that would reveal its fragility
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Primary driver — 'Confirmation bias makes it difficult for a team to identify the low likelihood of a sequential plan succeeding, as they only look for data points supporting their initial, optimistic hypothesis.'
admission_edge.source_description: Confirmation bias drives the fallacy by making the team collect only evidence that supports the optimistic sequential plan.
Conjunction-fallacy conflicts with commitment-bias when acknowledging that a multi-step plan is conjunctively fragile threatens consistency with the original commitment.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When complex multi-step plans need to be simplified to expose hidden assumptions and compounding probability risks that are invisible in the detailed narrative
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Diagnostic tool — 'forcing the user to distill complex ideas into simple terms and identify all blind spots' helps 'expose the shaky assumptions and compounding risks' in conjunctive plans. Operates as reveal mechanism rather than formal correction.
admission_edge.source_description: The Feynman Technique exposes weak assumptions and compounding risks by forcing the plan into simpler, checkable language.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When the first constraint identified is receiving disproportionate attention and the team is not testing whether a different constraint is actually the binding limit on the system
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Frame fixation — 'Over-focusing on an initial constraint or piece of information' — the first constraint identified absorbs disproportionate attention, preventing recognition of more binding limits.
admission_edge.source_description: Anchoring distorts constraints when the initial boundary gets over-weighted after the real problem or environment changes.
Constraints conflicts with lateral-thinking when imposed constraints channel thinking so narrowly that non-obvious solutions outside the constraint set are never considered.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When identified constraints need to be converted into repeatable operational procedures that ensure consistent enforcement across team members and situations
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Operational tool — 'The primary purpose of identifying and applying constraints' is served through checklist enforcement, turning constraints into repeatable execution discipline.
admission_edge.source_description: Checklists turn constraints into explicit operating boundaries so teams can focus on what belongs inside the frame.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When the feedback giver or receiver is filtering performance evidence through an existing narrative rather than genuinely engaging with data that disconfirms their current assessment
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Blocks honest assessment — 'demands openness to evidence that disconfirms one's current assessment' — causes feedback givers and receivers to filter evidence through existing narratives about performance.
admission_edge.source_description: Confirmation-bias makes constructive-feedback-models weaker by turning corrective evidence into something each side explains away instead of learning from.

Constructive-feedback-models conflicts with authority-bias when feedback delivery is shaped by the giver's rank rather than the quality of the observation, causing recipients to comply rather than learn.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When feedback delivery requires demonstrating genuine personal care and understanding of the recipient's perspective before the substantive critique can be received productively
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Relational foundation — 'care personally' — active listening creates the trust and attention that makes feedback receivable, but operates as a social prerequisite rather than a feedback-specific mechanism.
admission_edge.source_description: Active-listening helps constructive-feedback-models land because the receiver is more likely to hear correction when they feel accurately understood.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When the consulting team's analysis is being structured to confirm the initial hypothesis rather than using the methodology's rigor to genuinely test whether the hypothesis withstands scrutiny
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Methodology threat — 'risk of confirmation bias' — causes consulting teams to structure their analysis to confirm the initial hypothesis rather than genuinely testing it through the methodology's analytical rigor.
admission_edge.source_description: Confirmation-bias corrupts consulting-firms-methodology when the initial hypothesis becomes politically protected instead of rigorously tested.
Consulting-firms-methodology conflicts with empathy when framework-complete recommendations miss stakeholder adoption frictions.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When a complex problem needs to be structured into a MECE issue tree or logic framework before analysis can be distributed across team members and workstreams
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Core method — 'breaking it down into manageable parts' — decomposition IS the analytical engine of consulting methodology, providing the MECE issue trees and logic frameworks that structure the engagement.
admission_edge.source_description: Decomposition strengthens consulting-firms-methodology by turning vague issues into hypothesis-testable parts.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When a correlation that confirms the team's preferred causal story is being accepted without testing alternative explanations or seeking disconfirming evidence
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Directly interferes — 'Confirmation Bias directly interferes with accurate causal analysis' — causes teams to accept correlations that confirm their preferred causal story while ignoring alternative explanations.
admission_edge.source_description: Confirmation-bias interferes with causal diagnosis by filtering evidence toward the cause story the team already wants to believe.
Correlation-vs-causation conflicts with simplification when insistence on establishing causation blocks timely action in situations where strong correlation is the best available decision input.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When a correlation has been identified and controlled experimentation is needed to isolate the causal variable and rule out confounders before drawing causal conclusions
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Verification mechanism — 'Understanding causation drivers leads toward statistical analysis' and controlled experimentation — the empirical tool that definitively separates causal from correlational relationships.
admission_edge.source_description: Experimentation gives correlation-vs-causation a disciplined way to test whether the claimed driver actually produces the observed result.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When the actual outcome is anchoring the counterfactual analysis so that alternative scenarios cluster narrowly around what happened rather than exploring genuinely different trajectories
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Limits scenario range — 'This prevents anchoring (focusing too much on a single piece of information)' — the actual outcome becomes an anchor that constrains the range of counterfactual alternatives considered.
admission_edge.source_description: Anchoring works against counterfactual-reasoning when the first judgment or first shared view narrows the branch set too early.
Counterfactual-reasoning conflicts with confirmation-bias when teams search for support for the winning story instead of realistic alternatives.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When counterfactual alternatives need to be organized into a structured branching framework that makes it possible to compare the actual outcome against what would have happened under different choices
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Structural tool — 'allows decision-makers to view the outcome that occurred alongside alternative outcomes' — provides the branching framework for organizing counterfactual scenarios, but is a tool rather than the reasoning mode itself.
admission_edge.source_description: Decision-trees helps counterfactual-reasoning recover the missing branches that make the original choice intelligible.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When evidence of disruptive alternatives or incumbent structural weakness is being filtered to protect the existing structure because the team has a vested interest in its continuation
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Directly blocks creative destruction — 'confirmation bias leads teams to process information to get the conclusion they want' — causes incumbents to selectively interpret evidence to protect existing structures against disruptive alternatives.
admission_edge.source_description: Confirmation-bias blocks creative-destruction when teams defend the incumbent logic instead of killing their own wrong ideas.
Creative-destruction conflicts with commitment-bias when public prior strategy blocks timely reinvention.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When creative destruction requires stripping away the accumulated assumptions protecting an incumbent structure to reveal whether the underlying fundamentals still justify its existence
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Enabling mechanism — 'stripping away assumptions to leave only a set of facts and first principles' — first-principles thinking provides the intellectual foundation for creative destruction by removing the inherited assumptions that protect incumbent structures.
admission_edge.source_description: First-principles-thinking strengthens creative-destruction by stripping away inherited assumptions before building the replacement logic.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When early signals are interpreted as confirming threshold proximity without testing whether the situation actually exhibits critical-mass dynamics
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: From tensions analysis — pattern-recognition bias causes teams to force a threshold framing onto problems that do not actually follow critical-mass dynamics, misapplying the model rather than directly blocking it.
admission_edge.source_description: Confirmation-bias makes critical-mass overfit a threshold story onto weak evidence just because the team wants the pattern to be true.
Critical-mass conflicts with incentives when local actor payoffs discourage participation needed to reach threshold momentum.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When a system has crossed its threshold and positive feedback mechanisms need to be identified and leveraged to sustain momentum
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Described as 'directly relates to understanding how feedback loops operate' — once the critical threshold is met, positive feedback loops accelerate growth, making this the mechanism by which critical mass becomes self-sustaining.
