admission_edge.source_description: Confirmation-bias weakens latticework-of-mental-models when teams use many models cosmetically but still protect the worldview they already prefer.
Latticework-of-mental-models conflicts with simplification when accumulating frameworks adds analytical overhead that delays the simple decision one model alone would have reached.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When building or extending the latticework requires distinguishing foundational models from derivative ones by decomposing to fundamental truths
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: First-principles provides the decomposition method for building the latticework from foundational truths — strips away assumptions to reveal which core models anchor the structure.
admission_edge.source_description: First-principles-thinking helps latticework-of-mental-models avoid becoming a collection of elegant slogans by forcing reconstruction from fundamentals.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When a coherent narrative constructed from limited data points substitutes for the systematic large-sample evidence that LLN requires for reliable inference
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Narrative coherence produces 'exaggerated coherence' where System 1 constructs rich images from few scraps of evidence — compelling stories override the statistical discipline LLN demands.
admission_edge.source_description: Narratives can work against law-of-large-numbers when vivid stories seduce the team away from population logic.
Law-of-large-numbers conflicts with conjunction-fallacy when complex multi-step plans are treated as more likely than their compounded probabilities allow.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When base-rate estimates need to be trusted as stable population parameters rather than small-sample artifacts vulnerable to regression effects
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Described as deeply intertwined — 'reliable base rates must be derived from large samples' — LLN provides the statistical guarantee that base rates converge to true population parameters.
admission_edge.source_description: Base-rates operationalizes law-of-large-numbers by turning large-sample frequencies into usable priors for judgment.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When organizational inertia and traditional linear delivery processes resist the rapid iteration and pivoting that lean methodology demands
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Legacy delivery cadence blocks build-measure-learn iteration — LSM 'explicitly acknowledges that business systems are living systems not amenable to mechanical, step-by-step beliefs'.
admission_edge.source_description: Status-quo-bias pushes lean-startup-methodology back toward premature planning and continuation when evidence should force change.
Lean-startup-methodology conflicts with commitment-bias when founders keep scaling a cherished plan after real-world evidence weakens the original thesis.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When the build-measure-learn cycle requires genuine understanding of customer pain points rather than internal assumptions about what users need
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: LSM depends on deep customer empathy through its Design Thinking alliance — 'synthesizing qualitative data to build understanding' of customer needs drives the hypothesis formation process.
admission_edge.source_description: Empathy helps lean-startup-methodology measure the right user reality instead of optimizing a product around internal assumptions.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When current competence level feels adequate and the effort required to advance further on the learning curve is perceived as unnecessary disruption
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Resistance to engaging in effortful new learning when existing competence feels sufficient — status quo bias causes stagnation on the learning curve plateau.
admission_edge.source_description: Status-quo-bias weakens the learning-curve when an initially successful routine gets protected long after it should be updated or deepened.
Learning-curve conflicts with expertise-reversal-effect when support structures appropriate for early learning become counterproductive at higher competence levels.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When accumulated expertise needs to be systematized into reliable protocols to prevent regression and ensure consistent application of learned procedures
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: As mastery advances, 'checklists and protocols are required to handle sophisticated activities to reduce errors and ensure fundamental steps are not overlooked' — checklists preserve learning gains.
admission_edge.source_description: Checklists support the learning-curve by stabilizing routine steps so growing capability is not lost to preventable procedural errors.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When leverage point identification is driven by the analyst's preferred intervention rather than systematic sensitivity testing across the full system
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Focusing analysis only on data that supports the initial assumed leverage point rather than seeking disconfirming evidence — directly corrupts the identification process.
admission_edge.source_description: Confirmation-bias can make leverage-point selection reflect the analyst's preferred intervention instead of the system's real sensitivity.
Leverage-points conflicts with optionality when continuous branching delays commitment to the highest-impact intervention.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When conventional intervention approaches are low-leverage and finding the highest-impact point requires decomposing the problem to fundamental truths rather than following inherited frameworks
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Described as 'highly synergistic' — first-principles 'strips away assumptions to leave only core facts and desired outcomes, allowing the user to forge a new solution instead of following conventional, lower-leverage methods'.
admission_edge.source_description: First-principles-thinking helps leverage-points look beneath conventional surface fixes to the deeper system element that truly governs outcomes.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When a liked authority figure's recommendations receive lower evidentiary scrutiny because both social warmth and status suppress the impulse to challenge
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Social warmth and status jointly bypass critical scrutiny — when liking and authority combine, the double influence makes evidence standards dangerously low.
admission_edge.source_description: Authority-bias combines dangerously with liking-principle when status and warmth together reduce skepticism toward a favored messenger.
Liking-principle conflicts with confirmation-bias when favorable messengers receive lower evidentiary standards.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When the liking principle needs a foundation of genuine trust and safety rather than operating as surface-level social manipulation
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Psychological safety provides the environment where liking can function authentically — trust and engagement are built when people feel safe to express genuine warmth and connection.
admission_edge.source_description: Psychological-safety helps liking-principle lower defensiveness without reducing candor, making hard recommendations easier to hear.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When defaulting to time-tested approaches becomes reflexive rather than deliberate, blocking exploration of novel solutions that may be superior in changed contexts
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Lindy's preference for proven approaches can devolve into availability heuristic — 'using the handy framework you know' or substitution bias when facing genuinely novel problems.
admission_edge.source_description: Einstellung-effect undermines lindy-effect by causing practitioners to default to a known long-lived framework simply because it is readily available, substituting familiarity for fit when the problem is genuinely novel.
Lindy-effect conflicts with black-swan-events when rare discontinuities can abruptly end a long-lived baseline.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When turning beneficial lock-in patterns into explicit, repeatable operational structures that do not depend on rediscovering the routine each time
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Practical tool for operationalizing beneficial lock-in ('locks work processes into consistent, repeatable patterns') — a tool-level relationship rather than the deeper mechanism that cognitive-load-theory provides.
admission_edge.source_description: Checklists turn beneficial lock-in into explicit repeatable structure so execution does not depend on rediscovering the routine each time.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When inherited processes or conventions persist through inertia rather than because they have been re-derived from fundamental requirements
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Directly breaks unhealthy lock-in — 'explicitly breaks the lock of convention by stripping away assumptions to leave only fundamental facts and the desired outcome.'
admission_edge.source_description: First-principles-thinking breaks unhealthy lock-in by stripping away inherited convention and asking what the path would look like from fundamental facts.
Lock-in conflicts with optionality when irreversible commitments eliminate adaptive branch choices.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When turning beneficial lock-in patterns into explicit, repeatable operational structures that do not depend on rediscovering the routine each time
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Practical tool for operationalizing beneficial lock-in ('locks work processes into consistent, repeatable patterns') — a tool-level relationship rather than the deeper mechanism that cognitive-load-theory provides.
admission_edge.source_description: Checklists turn beneficial lock-in into explicit repeatable structure so execution does not depend on rediscovering the routine each time.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When the desire to confirm a preferred conclusion causes fallacious reasoning to be accepted as valid because it supports the desired outcome
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Described as 'persistent and dangerous' — confirmation bias causes problem solvers to ignore evidence that challenges preconceptions, directly enabling logical fallacies to go undetected.
admission_edge.source_description: Confirmation-bias drives logical fallacies by protecting the desired conclusion instead of the valid inference.
Logical-fallacies conflicts with narratives when compelling narrative coherence is mistaken for logical soundness and fallacy detection is suspended.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When evaluating claims requires both detecting logical errors in the argument structure and ensuring the claims are empirically testable and falsifiable
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Fallacy identification 'directly supports Falsifiability by helping to identify and reconcile disconfirming evidence' — mutual reinforcement between logical rigor and scientific testability.
admission_edge.source_description: Falsifiability strengthens logical-fallacies detection by forcing claims to survive disconfirming evidence rather than rhetorical confidence.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When safety margin estimates are derived from data selected to validate the current plan rather than from adversarial stress-testing
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Prevents acknowledgment of potential failure modes — selects safety estimates that confirm the current exposure is acceptable rather than stress-testing honestly against adverse scenarios.
admission_edge.source_description: Confirmation-bias undermines margin-of-safety by selecting a safety estimate that confirms the current exposure is acceptable.
Margin-of-safety conflicts with feedback-loops when delayed signals create false confidence in thin buffers.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When sizing protective buffers requires quantifying uncertainty distributions rather than relying on best-case or point-estimate forecasts
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Described as 'quantifying the uncertainty that necessitates the margin' — provides the quantitative foundation for evidence-based buffer sizing, making the margin rational rather than arbitrary.
admission_edge.source_description: Probabilistic-thinking helps margin-of-safety size the buffer from realistic uncertainty instead of the cleanest forecast path.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When sequential rigor and structured analysis constrain the creative exploration needed to discover non-obvious state transitions or reframe the problem space entirely
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: The highly structured sequential nature 'can oppose creativity, which relies on free-form recombination of ideas' — divergent thinking requires the diffuse mode that structured models constrain.
admission_edge.source_description: Divergent-vs-convergent-thinking undermines markov-chains by demanding free-form recombination of ideas that cannot be captured in a fixed sequence of discrete states, breaking the structured progression the model depends on.
Markov-chains conflicts with optionality when the state space branches faster than the transition evidence can support.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When sequential state transitions need to be evaluated probabilistically using structured decision frameworks rather than intuitive path estimates
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Supports quantitative prediction through 'Bayesian statistics and Monte Carlo simulation' — decision trees provide the structured probability framework for transition analysis.
admission_edge.source_description: Decision-trees help markov-chains expose explicit branches and state transitions instead of leaving the sequence implicit.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When mental models become entrenched worldviews that filter out disconfirming evidence rather than being treated as provisional tools subject to revision
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: MMs 'reinforce the tendency to seek, interpret, and favor information that confirms pre-existing beliefs, shielding the ego from uncomfortable truths and hindering learning' — calcifies models and prevents updating.
admission_edge.source_description: Confirmation-bias protects an existing map of reality even when disconfirming evidence should update it.
Mental-models-of-reality conflicts with first-principles-thinking when inherited abstractions block decomposition to fundamentals.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When mental simulation needs to be organized into structured outcome branches with explicit probability estimates rather than free-form scenario imagination
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Decision trees provide structured frameworks for organizing simulation outcomes — 'visualization to conceptualize solutions before implementation' benefits from branching probability structures.
admission_edge.source_description: Decision-trees help mental-simulation compare multiple branches and threshold-triggered outcomes instead of following only one imagined path.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When prior investment in a course of action creates pressure to dismiss simulation results that suggest the current plan should be abandoned
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: When simulation 'challenges a deeply held belief or a prior commitment, cognitive pressure can lead to the rejection of objective simulation results' — commitment corrupts interpretation.
admission_edge.source_description: Commitment-bias interferes with mental-simulation when prior plans create pressure to reject simulated outcomes that challenge the current course.
Mental-simulation conflicts with confirmation-bias when rehearsed futures reinforce existing beliefs instead of pressure-testing them.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When mental simulation needs to be organized into structured outcome branches with explicit probability estimates rather than free-form scenario imagination
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Decision trees provide structured frameworks for organizing simulation outcomes — 'visualization to conceptualize solutions before implementation' benefits from branching probability structures.
admission_edge.source_description: Decision-trees help mental-simulation compare multiple branches and threshold-triggered outcomes instead of following only one imagined path.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When self-monitoring is used to rationalize existing beliefs rather than genuinely examining whether the reasoning process is producing accurate rather than comfortable conclusions
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: MCR 'struggles against the deeply ingrained human instinct to dismiss new, disconfirming information and instead seek data that validates existing beliefs' — directly opposes the open inquiry MCR demands.
admission_edge.source_description: Confirmation-bias weakens meta-cognitive-reflection by making the self-audit protect the current story instead of revising it.
Meta-cognitive-reflection conflicts with emotional-intelligence when introspective analysis delays timely relational response.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When critical analysis needs self-aware monitoring of its own reasoning process to detect when assumptions are being treated as facts
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Described as 'Critical thinking is rooted in MCR' — MCR provides the self-awareness foundation to question assumptions, evaluate evidence, and separate facts from beliefs.
admission_edge.source_description: Critical-thinking gives meta-cognitive-reflection a sharper evaluative standard so self-observation improves judgment instead of becoming narrative about the self.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When initial assumptions or prominent data points narrow the questioning process before alternative framings and broader inquiry have been attempted
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Anchoring constrains the question space MCQ explores — initial framing or data points narrow inquiry before the full space of relevant questions has been explored.
admission_edge.source_description: Anchoring weakens metacognitive questioning when the first framing or answer keeps pulling the inquiry back to the same assumptions.
Metacognitive-questioning conflicts with confidence-calibration when constant questioning produces paralytic doubt that undermines well-founded judgments.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When evidence evaluation requires structured self-inquiry to detect when reasoning is being driven by assumptions rather than verified premises
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: MCQ is a core critical thinking tool — the canonical describes it as 'essential for evaluating evidence and questioning assumptions' through structured self-inquiry.
admission_edge.source_description: Critical-thinking turns metacognitive questioning into disciplined probing of evidence, assumptions, and argumentative weak spots.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When sophisticated simulation output creates false confidence in precise probability estimates that are ultimately only as reliable as the subjective inputs that seeded them
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Monte Carlo distributions can 'create an illusion of precision around fundamentally unquantifiable inputs' — computational rigor can mask input uncertainty.
admission_edge.source_description: False-precision-avoidance protects monte-carlo-methods from projecting exactness that the input assumptions have not earned.
Monte-carlo-methods conflicts with simplification when simulation complexity obscures the dominant variables a simpler closed-form analysis would reveal.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When simulation inputs need to be anchored in empirical frequency data rather than subjective estimates to prevent garbage-in-garbage-out distortion
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Monte Carlo requires 'grounding probability estimates in history, external data, and the experience of others through reference classes' — base rates provide the foundational input distributions.
admission_edge.source_description: Base-rates ground monte-carlo-methods in reference classes so simulated inputs are not built from wishful stories alone.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When agents protected from downside risk use motivated reasoning to justify risk-taking rather than honestly assessing whether their actions externalize harm
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Under moral hazard protection, agents are susceptible to motivated reasoning — 'smart people are particularly good at spinning narratives to justify their choices' when shielded from consequences.
admission_edge.source_description: Confirmation-bias worsens moral-hazard analysis when protected actors and reviewers alike accept narratives that rationalize hidden risk-taking.
Moral-hazard conflicts with adverse-selection when both models describe information asymmetry but the real difference is post-contract behavior versus pre-contract filtering.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When protected agents are making decisions that externalize risk, and the root cause is misaligned reward structures rather than individual bad faith
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Moral hazard IS fundamentally an incentive misalignment problem — described as 'the negative outcome of poorly calibrated consequences' where incentive design is 'essential to engineering a system that mitigates this risk'.
admission_edge.source_description: Incentives is the direct partner model that helps moral-hazard turn hidden risk-taking into a redesign problem around consequence alignment.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When prior commitment to a preferred option causes criteria weights to be unconsciously manipulated to confirm the pre-existing preference rather than genuinely evaluating alternatives
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Scoring weights get 'frozen around an already favored option' — commitment bias corrupts the mechanism that makes MCDA useful by steering criteria toward predetermined conclusions.
admission_edge.source_description: Commitment-bias distorts multi-criteria-decision-analysis when the matrix is reverse-engineered to defend a preferred option.
Multi-criteria-decision-analysis conflicts with representativeness-heuristic when salient criteria overshadow base-rate relevance.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When multi-criteria evaluation needs structured branching frameworks to organize alternatives and criteria rather than holistic intuitive comparison
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Decision trees provide structured analytical frameworks for MCDA — hypothesis-driven problem solving 'ensures that analysis will unambiguously resolve an issue' through defined criteria.
admission_edge.source_description: Decision-trees strengthens multi-criteria-decision-analysis by making branches, outcomes, and trade-offs explicit before scoring.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When domain experts on the team communicate at abstraction levels that prevent knowledge transfer across cultural and disciplinary boundaries
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Described as 'a major barrier to effective cross-disciplinary communication within a diverse team' — experts jump to abstraction, making communication incomprehensible to those outside their specialization.
admission_edge.source_description: Curse-of-knowledge undermines multicultural-team-dynamics by causing specialists to communicate at an abstraction level incomprehensible to colleagues from other disciplines, nullifying the cross-pollination that diversity is designed to enable.
Multicultural-team-dynamics conflicts with authority-bias when hierarchy overrides lower-power cross-cultural signal.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When diverse team interactions require managing emotional and cultural friction rather than just exchanging analytical content
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Emotional competence is described as 'necessary for success, particularly in roles involving coordination and group dynamics' — EQ enables management of the affective dimension of cross-cultural disagreements.
admission_edge.source_description: Empathy strengthens multicultural-team-dynamics by helping the team model how the same event looks from different cultural standpoints.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When the story selectively includes evidence that supports the desired conclusion while omitting contradictory data that would weaken narrative coherence
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Narrative coherence is 'constructed by selectively including supporting evidence and omitting disconfirming data' — confirmation bias directly corrupts narrative construction and interpretation.
admission_edge.source_description: Confirmation-bias intensifies narratives when rhetorical skill is used to defend a desired conclusion rather than test it.
Narratives conflicts with base-rates when a compelling story overrides statistical frequency data that should anchor the estimate.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When complex information needs to be compressed into memorable patterns that audiences can absorb and recall without requiring deep domain expertise
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Narratives compress complex reality into memorable story patterns — schemas and abstractions provide the cognitive shortcuts that make stories instantly understandable and transferable.
admission_edge.source_description: Abstraction helps narratives compress complex facts into a clear causal line without making the audience hold every detail at once.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When real-world decision-makers use intuitive shortcuts and emotional heuristics rather than the rational computation that Nash Equilibrium assumes
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: NE 'assumes perfectly rational agents — this clashes directly with the reality of bounded rationality' where humans rely on mental shortcuts leading to predictable errors that NE cannot account for.
admission_edge.source_description: System-1 undermines nash-equilibrium by bypassing the cold rational analysis required to compute equilibrium payoffs, substituting primal emotional responses that distort strategic assessment.
Nash-equilibrium conflicts with confirmation-bias when analysts model payoffs to confirm a preferred equilibrium instead of mapping the game honestly.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When computing equilibria requires structured sequential analysis of strategy-payoff combinations rather than intuitive assessment of likely outcomes
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Analyzing payoffs and strategies 'often involves disaggregating the problem structure, such as using deductive logic trees' — decision trees structure the sequential analysis NE computation requires.
admission_edge.source_description: Decision-trees help nash-equilibrium lay out strategic branches and countermoves clearly enough to inspect.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When drawing lessons from evolutionary outcomes focuses only on surviving entities while ignoring the vastly larger population of failures that were selected against
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Survivorship bias directly corrupts conclusions drawn from natural selection by hiding the failure data — we see only survivors, not the failures that selection eliminated, creating false lessons about success factors.
admission_edge.source_description: Survivorship-bias distorts natural-selection-analogy when analysts study only the winners and ignore what failed variants would have revealed.
Natural-selection-analogy conflicts with second-order-thinking when "survival of the fittest" framing ignores second-order consequences like monoculture fragility or systemic brittleness.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When generating the variety of options that selection can act upon requires structured experimentation rather than theoretical prediction
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Iterative improvement 'directly implements the selection/retention loop' — experimentation generates the variations that natural selection operates upon.
admission_edge.source_description: Experimentation operationalizes natural-selection-analogy by generating variants and letting evidence eliminate weak options.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When network product complexity creates cognitive barriers to adoption that prevent new users from experiencing the network value proposition
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Overloading the audience's working memory 'hinders the assimilation of new information' — complexity is a practical barrier to the rapid adoption network effects require.
admission_edge.source_description: Cognitive-load-theory conflicts with network-effects when a complex product explanation overloads the audience before adoption can spread.
Network-effects conflicts with base-rates when projected network growth extrapolates without accounting for historical failure rates of platforms that never reached critical mass.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When network growth dynamics depend on reaching a specific adoption threshold below which the network provides insufficient value to attract new participants
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Network effects are defined by the critical mass threshold that triggers self-reinforcing growth — without reaching critical mass, network effects remain latent and the system cannot achieve self-sustaining adoption.
admission_edge.source_description: Critical-mass gives network-effects its threshold logic by marking the point where participation becomes self-sustaining.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When simplifying assumptions reduce a genuinely non-linear system to a linear model, eliminating the threshold effects and feedback dynamics that drive actual system behavior
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Linearized approximations destroy the non-linear information that makes the dynamics meaningful — 'small input changes produce disproportionate output shifts' in genuinely non-linear systems.
admission_edge.source_description: Simplification undermines non-linear-dynamics by linearizing approximations in systems where small input changes produce disproportionate output shifts, masking the feedback loops and emergent properties the model exists to reveal.
Non-linear-dynamics conflicts with risk-vs-uncertainty when leaders act as if unstable feedback systems were just ordinary forecastable risk.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When system outputs are disproportionate to inputs because feedback mechanisms amplify or dampen signals in ways that create threshold effects and phase transitions
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Feedback loops ARE the mechanism that creates non-linear behavior — 'essential mechanisms for continuous improvement' that drive the amplification and dampening cycles producing non-linear outputs.
admission_edge.source_description: Feedback-loops supply the concrete reinforcing and balancing structure that makes non-linear dynamics decision-useful.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When power dynamics prevent the open, bidirectional needs-and-observations exchange that non-violent communication requires
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Role power suppresses direct needs-and-observations exchange — authority bias causes lower-power participants to withhold authentic communication to avoid challenging hierarchical expectations.
admission_edge.source_description: Authority-bias undermines non-violent-communication when role power suppresses direct observation-and-needs exchange.
Non-violent-communication conflicts with confirmation-bias when rigid adherence to one's own interpretation blocks the open, non-judgmental listening that the model requires.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When communication requires genuine honesty about needs and observations rather than strategic impression management or diplomatic avoidance
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Radical Transparency/Truth 'aligns perfectly with the model's focus on honesty in communication' — authenticity provides the disposition that makes non-violent communication genuine rather than manipulative.
admission_edge.source_description: Authenticity helps non-violent-communication surface real experience and tension instead of keeping the exchange in impression-management mode.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When evidence of control gaps creates psychological discomfort that leads to rationalization of the existing mapping rather than honest gap acknowledgment
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: If a flaw is revealed in the OCM, 'dissonance makes it psychologically difficult to abandon or critique the existing framework' — resistance to updating established mappings.
admission_edge.source_description: Cognitive-dissonance resists OCM revision by making it psychologically painful to acknowledge flaws in an existing mapping — the discomfort of inconsistency between 'I built this framework' and 'this framework has a gap' drives motivated distortion rather than honest updating.
Obligations-controls-mapping conflicts with authority-bias when documented control exceptions pass without evidence review.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When the obligation-control mapping becomes too complex to hold in working memory and needs to be chunked into cognitively manageable units
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: OCM's emphasis on 'breaking down tasks into small, manageable steps aligns directly with the brain's limitation of processing only a few pieces of new information in working memory'.
admission_edge.source_description: Cognitive Load Theory supports OCM by forcing control design into manageable steps that people can actually follow.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When preference for simplicity causes selective evidence gathering that confirms the simpler hypothesis while ignoring data requiring a more complex explanation
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Seeking evidence that supports the preferred simpler hypothesis while overlooking disconfirming information that might introduce necessary complexity.
admission_edge.source_description: Confirmation-bias corrupts Occam's Razor when the thinker chooses the simpler story because it feels congenial, not because it best fits the evidence.

Occam's-razor conflicts with representativeness-heuristic when story simplicity and causal accuracy pull apart — the representativeness heuristic makes the most familiar pattern feel like the most parsimonious explanation, displacing the evidence-based test the razor requires.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When explanatory or analytical complexity exceeds working memory capacity and needs to be reduced to enable effective processing and schema formation
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: OR 'supports the application of this theory by emphasizing simplicity and chunking, thereby reducing the mental energy required for working memory to assimilate new information'.
admission_edge.source_description: Cognitive-load-theory complements Occam's Razor because pruning unnecessary complexity reduces the mental burden that makes weak explanations feel harder to test.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When the assessment of foregone alternatives is biased by preference for the current option rather than honest evaluation of what is being sacrificed
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Confirmation bias 'obstructs the objective assessment of opportunity cost' by making one reluctant to recognize the potential benefits of unfavored alternatives.
admission_edge.source_description: Confirmation-bias obstructs opportunity-cost by making an unfavored alternative hard to assess objectively.
Opportunity-cost conflicts with anchoring when the comparison is pinned to the wrong baseline instead of the best real alternative.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When evaluating an opportunity requires decomposing past the surface value proposition to compare against fundamentally different alternatives
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: OC 'forces the strip-down of conventional assumptions' by requiring objective comparison to alternatives — 'Compared to what?' aids in forging solutions based on facts rather than convention.
admission_edge.source_description: First-principles-thinking helps opportunity-cost strip away inherited assumptions and compare alternatives against real fundamentals.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When confidence in the plan stems from ego and the inside view rather than genuine evidence, and the decision-maker needs to acknowledge what they don't know
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Intellectual humility 'actively combats' overoptimism by motivating the decision-maker to worry that they might not be seeing choices optimally, forcing exploration of contradictory viewpoints.
admission_edge.source_description: Intellectual-humility is a direct antagonist because it makes the planner worry they may not be seeing the choice optimally and forces real updating.
Optimism-bias-and-planning-fallacy conflicts with commitment-bias when optimistic forecasts become anchors that commitment pressure prevents from being revised downward.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When optimistic project planning needs structured adversarial testing to surface the neglected threats and systemic issues that overconfidence hides
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Premortems channel optimism bias into productive risk assessment — structured failure imagination helps manage the bias by forcing explicit consideration of disaster scenarios before commitment.
admission_edge.source_description: Premortem gives optimism-bias-and-planning-fallacy a direct correction path by forcing downside imagination before commitment.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When the optimization target has been set and the team selectively gathers evidence that the current approach is optimal while ignoring signs of suboptimality
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Team members may feel pressure to confirm the optimization hypothesis rather than challenging it skeptically — optimization targets become self-confirming.
admission_edge.source_description: Confirmation-bias makes optimization feel rigorous while quietly protecting the current objective, proxy, or favored frame from real challenge.
Optimization-theory conflicts with non-linear-dynamics when optimization assumes smooth response surfaces in systems with discontinuous phase transitions.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When optimization efforts need to respect real-world boundaries rather than pursuing theoretical optima that violate system constraints
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Constraints define the solution space within which optimization operates — understanding cognitive limits (CLT), competitive boundaries (game theory), and structural boundaries shapes what optimal means.
admission_edge.source_description: Constraints give optimization its real boundary conditions so the best option is defined by actual limits rather than by idealized freedom.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When prior investment or public commitment creates escalation pressure that forecloses objectively superior alternatives because pivoting feels like failure
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Commitment makes it 'extremely difficult to pivot or consider new, better options' — psychological pressure from prior choices directly destroys the flexibility optionality requires.
admission_edge.source_description: Commitment-and-consistency-bias makes optionality psychologically expensive because prior choices become harder to revisit even when better paths appear.
Optionality conflicts with prioritization when keeping all options open prevents the ruthless elimination that focused execution requires.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When the value of maintaining versus exercising options needs to be evaluated through structured analysis of branching outcomes and their probabilities
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Decision trees map the branching possibilities that optionality maintains — structured pathway analysis helps evaluate when to exercise versus preserve options.
admission_edge.source_description: Decision-trees help optionality model branching choices and probabilistic outcomes instead of treating the future as one track.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When the highest-leverage 20% of factors identified by Pareto analysis falls outside the decision-maker's sphere of influence or organizational authority
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: High-impact levers identified by Pareto may sit outside current execution authority — the gap between what is impactful and what is controllable limits practical application.
admission_edge.source_description: Circle-of-control resists Pareto when the highest-impact levers sit outside execution authority and the model starts optimizing imaginary influence.
Pareto-principle conflicts with confirmation-bias when the vital-few selection confirms already-favored priorities instead of coming from an independent impact analysis.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When the search for high-impact intervention points can be guided by empirical distribution analysis showing which inputs disproportionately drive outputs
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Identifying the vital 20% that produces 80% of results IS finding leverage points in the outcome distribution — Pareto and leverage points are complementary identification mechanisms.
admission_edge.source_description: Leverage-points gives Pareto its search target by identifying the small set of factors most likely to move the outcome disproportionately.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When the inherited path constrains solution design to incremental variants while first-principles analysis reveals fundamentally superior alternatives requiring path abandonment
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Path dependence relies on following conventional means while first-principles 'strips away all assumptions and precedents, reducing the problem to fundamental facts to forge a new, potentially divergent solution'.
admission_edge.source_description: First-principles-thinking breaks path-dependence by stripping away inherited route assumptions and rebuilding from the underlying facts.
Path-dependence conflicts with confirmation-bias when decision-makers selectively credit evidence that justifies staying on the current path rather than fairly evaluating the case for switching.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When understanding why certain options are unavailable requires tracing which past decisions created the structural constraints that currently bind the system
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Constraints ARE the mechanism through which path dependence operates — prior commitments and investments create structural constraints that limit available future states.
admission_edge.source_description: Constraints help path-dependence become visible by showing how inherited standards, interfaces, and dependencies narrow the real option set.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When the credibility of peer feedback is weighted by organizational status rather than relevant expertise and evidence quality
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Peer review degrades when it 'defers to the highest-status reviewer rather than weighting evidence quality independently' — authority bias corrupts the merit-based evaluation PRYP demands.
admission_edge.source_description: Authority-bias weakens peer-review-your-perspectives when status determines which critiques count and which viewpoints are never allowed to challenge the frame.
Peer-review-your-perspectives conflicts with confirmation-bias when reviewers selected from the same paradigm reinforce shared blind spots instead of challenging them.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When analytical blind spots require external feedback to surface because self-monitoring alone cannot detect what the current framework systematically misses
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: PRYP IS a feedback loop for perspective correction — the peer review process provides the external signal that enables continuous improvement of one's own analytical framework.
admission_edge.source_description: Feedback-loops turn peer review into an actual correction mechanism instead of a one-time opinion exchange.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When expert-level pattern recognition creates difficulty communicating insights to novice audiences.
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Canonical: 'experts find it difficult to remember what it was like *not* to know something' — high-level abstraction hinders novice communication.
admission_edge.source_description: Curse-of-knowledge undermines perceptual-learning by making refined perceptual schemas impossible to communicate to novices, blocking the transfer of expert pattern recognition that the model is built to enable.
Perceptual-learning conflicts with confirmation-bias when prior pattern expectations suppress anomaly detection.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When complex information needs to be chunked into manageable patterns to reduce working memory demand.
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Canonical: 'PL reduces cognitive load' by developing stable patterns and chunks, freeing working memory for new schema formation.
admission_edge.source_description: Cognitive-load-theory supports perceptual-learning by freeing working memory so meaningful cues can consolidate into usable patterns.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When rigid persistence in a familiar approach prevents adoption of more effective strategies.
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Canonical risks: 'Inertia / Doubling Down — refusing to quit a failing course of action' due to rigid persistence in familiar approaches.
admission_edge.source_description: Einstellung-effect undermines persistence-grit by channeling sustained effort into a familiar but inappropriate framework, turning grit into stubborn repetition of the wrong approach.
Persistence-grit conflicts with commitment-bias when identity-level resolve blocks a needed strategic pivot.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When persistence must be directed through structured, focused practice to build genuine expertise.
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Canonical: Deep Work (close cousin of deliberate practice) 'requires the ability to concentrate without distraction'; grit provides the stamina for persistent engagement.
admission_edge.source_description: Deliberate-practice gives persistence-grit a structured way to turn endurance into improvement rather than mere repetition.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When deliberate System 2 analysis would reveal persuasive framing as manipulative or logically weak.
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Canonical: 'Persuasion aims for fast, automatic compliance (System 1). Critical thinking requires slow, deliberate evaluation of evidence and assumptions' — structural opposition.
admission_edge.source_description: Critical-thinking slows persuasion-principles down by asking whether the message is merely effective or actually well grounded.
Persuasion-principles conflicts with authenticity when strategic framing of a message compromises the transparency required for durable trust.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When crafting messages requires deep understanding of the audience's motives, fears, and desires.
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Canonical: 'Understanding the audience's motives and feelings (Theory of Mind) is crucial for packaging the message correctly' — essential for resonance.
admission_edge.source_description: Empathy helps persuasion-principles tune the message to what the audience actually cares about rather than to what the expert wants to say.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When organizational commitment to a promotion decision prevents acknowledging that the promoted person is mismatched to the role.
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Medium confidence: organizational commitment to promotion decisions can prevent acknowledging role mismatch, but not the primary antagonist in canonical.
admission_edge.source_description: Commitment-and-consistency-bias can keep organizations defending a promotion decision after capability mismatch becomes visible.
Peter-principle conflicts with growth-mindset when growth mindset assumes anyone can learn their way out of role incompetence at every hierarchical level.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When mapping which party controls the operational payoff, the next move, or the real outside option in a power relationship
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Complementary framing — 'together they explain why formal authority often loses' — but not described as the primary or essential mechanism for power-dynamics analysis.
admission_edge.source_description: Incentives explain why nominal authority can lose to the actor controlling the operational payoff, the next move, or the real fallback lane.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When assessing relative bargaining position and the team's evidence for its outside option has not been independently tested
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Directly distorts the core leverage analysis — makes teams see the leverage structure they want rather than the outside option evidence actually supports.
admission_edge.source_description: Confirmation-bias distorts power-dynamics by making teams see the leverage structure they want rather than the outside option they actually have.
Power-laws conflicts with base-rates when power-law distributions make average-based forecasts misleading because the mean is dominated by extreme values.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When mapping which party controls the operational payoff, the next move, or the real outside option in a power relationship
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Complementary framing — 'together they explain why formal authority often loses' — but not described as the primary or essential mechanism for power-dynamics analysis.
admission_edge.source_description: Incentives explain why nominal authority can lose to the actor controlling the operational payoff, the next move, or the real fallback lane.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When favored hypotheses about the 'critical few' prevent objective identification of true high-impact factors.
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Canonical risks: 'Confirmation Bias / Authority Bias: Jumping to a solution because it aligns with a favored hypothesis' about the critical few.
admission_edge.source_description: Confirmation-bias can make power-laws lock onto a preferred 20 percent before the evidence justifies it.
Power-laws conflicts with base-rates when power-law distributions make average-based forecasts misleading because the mean is dominated by extreme values.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When finding high-impact intervention points where concentrated effort produces disproportionate results.
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Canonical: power laws serve as 'critical filter for mental energy and resource focus' — leverage points identify where concentrated effort produces disproportionate results.
admission_edge.source_description: Leverage-points helps power-laws focus on the few variables whose movement changes the whole system.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When pre-suasive framing creates motivated reasoning that undermines objective hypothesis testing and evidence evaluation.
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Canonical tension: 'priming a favorable associative pattern leads to motivated reasoning that undermines rigorous hypothesis testing' — structural opposition.
admission_edge.source_description: Scientific-method-evidence-testing resists pre-suasion when associative priming starts substituting for rigorous evidence and hypothesis checking.
Premortem conflicts with commitment-bias when publicly stated positions harden into escalation-of-commitment and teams reinterpret disconfirming signals as temporary noise.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When understanding the target audience's perspective is essential for calibrating the pre-suasive context.
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Canonical: 'Having a strong theory of mind is essential for Pre-Suasion' — enables tuning the message to the target audience's perspective.
admission_edge.source_description: Empathy helps pre-suasion tune the preliminary frame to the audience's actual concerns rather than to the speaker's assumptions.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When the team has already publicly committed to the plan and sunk cost makes reversing feel psychologically costly
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Strong specific mechanism — publicly stated positions harden into escalation-of-commitment, making genuine failure exploration feel like disloyalty precisely when backward analysis is most needed.
admission_edge.source_description: Commitment-bias hardens public commitment into escalation, making it harder for a premortem to bind reversal triggers before more sunk cost accumulates.
Premortem conflicts with confirmation-bias when teams keep defending the favored plan instead of using the simulated failure to force genuine antithesis.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When structuring premortem findings into a repeatable pre-commitment control rather than relying on ad-hoc discussion quality
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Extracted from mitigations section, not the Latticework ally table — described as a supplementary tool for analytic rigor rather than a core synergy mechanism for premortem's backward-from-failure reasoning.
admission_edge.source_description: Checklists help premortem turn risk surfacing into a repeatable pre-commitment control instead of an improvised discussion.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When belief in standardized pricing prevents recognizing that different markets demand different prices.
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Canonical: 'makes people process information to get the conclusion they *want* rather than discovering what is true (that different markets demand different prices)'.
admission_edge.source_description: Confirmation-bias can make price-discrimination defend a preferred pricing structure instead of testing what buyers actually value.
Price-discrimination conflicts with prospect-theory when reference-price anchoring causes consumers to perceive differentiated pricing as unfair loss rather than rational segmentation.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When setting initial reference prices that shape subsequent perceptions of value and willingness to pay.
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Canonical: 'Setting an initial, high reference point (the anchor) significantly influences the perception of subsequent prices' — core pricing mechanism.
admission_edge.source_description: Anchoring gives price-discrimination a way to shape perceived value before the final price is judged.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When principals assume their initial hypothesis about agent performance is correct without rigorous testing.
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Canonical risks: 'Premature Analysis/Confirmation Bias — the Principal rushes into analysis without being crystal clear about the output needed'.
admission_edge.source_description: Confirmation-bias makes principal-agent-problem harder to diagnose because leaders can mistake mandate defense and dashboard compliance for genuine alignment.
Principal-agent-problem conflicts with information-asymmetry when the knowledge gap itself becomes the mechanism that hides divergence between principal goals and agent behavior.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When designing mechanisms to align agent behavior with principal objectives through reward and accountability structures.
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Incentive alignment IS the core solution to principal-agent problems. Canonical: orchestrating people and designs to align behavior with objectives.
admission_edge.source_description: Incentives is the direct partner model that helps principal-agent-problem translate hidden divergence into a redesign of consequences and rewards.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When existing beliefs or hypotheses bias the selection of priorities over objective assessment of alternatives.
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Canonical: 'The tendency to prioritize or seek out information that confirms existing beliefs. This directly conflicts with objective prioritization.'
admission_edge.source_description: Confirmation bias blocks objective prioritization by making the team overweight the evidence that fits its current hypothesis.
Prioritization conflicts with optionality when aggressive prioritization forecloses options that would have been valuable under high uncertainty.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When simplifying and chunking information is needed to surface the most important priority for the audience.
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Canonical: 'deliberately works *with* the brain's limitations' — breaking information into chunks reduces cognitive load to surface the core priority.
admission_edge.source_description: Cognitive Load Theory supports prioritization by reducing information overload and making the core priority memorable.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When players interpret ambiguous moves to confirm defection assumptions, accelerating mutual betrayal even when cooperation was intended.
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Canonical: 'Focusing solely on the competitive frame (betrayal as dominant strategy) without exploring alternative cooperative structures' when initial hypothesis is ingrained.
admission_edge.source_description: Confirmation-bias worsens prisoners-dilemma dynamics when ambiguous moves are read as confirming that the other side is defecting.
Prisoners-dilemma conflicts with active-listening when incentive structures reward concealment over transparent coordination.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When analyzing how payoff incentives drive cooperative or defective behavior in strategic interdependence scenarios.
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Incentive structures are central to PD dynamics — the payoff matrix IS an incentive structure. Canonical: outcome 'changes drastically' depending on how incentives frame cooperation vs defection.
admission_edge.source_description: Incentives helps prisoners-dilemma reveal when individually rational behavior is being produced by a payoff structure that rewards defection.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When existing beliefs distort probability estimates by selectively seeking confirming rather than disconfirming evidence.
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Canonical: 'This bias represents a failure of critical thinking, where people seek information that confirms existing beliefs. PT requires intellectual humility to identify disconfirming evidence.'
admission_edge.source_description: Confirmation-bias corrupts probabilistic-thinking by treating belief defense as if it were evidence weighting.
Probabilistic-thinking conflicts with narratives when story coherence makes a scenario feel more probable than its base rate warrants, overriding distributional reasoning.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When decisions require weighting outcomes by their probabilities to determine optimal expected returns.
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Expected value IS a core probabilistic calculation — fundamental mathematical tool for weighing outcomes by their probabilities. Intrinsic relationship.
admission_edge.source_description: Expected-value gives probabilistic-thinking an operational way to compare choices with mixed upside and downside instead of hunting for certainty.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When an initial frame anchors subsequent analysis so strongly that alternative frames are never seriously tested.
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Canonical risks: 'Focusing too much on a single, salient piece of information (the anchor)' — root cause of the hammer-and-nail problem in framing.
admission_edge.source_description: Anchoring becomes an antagonist when the first framing or salient cue keeps the team from testing alternative boundaries and causal structures.
Problem-framing-and-reframing conflicts with confirmation-bias when reframing is constrained to preferred hypotheses.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When selecting or evaluating a problem frame requires reflective awareness of one's own reasoning process and assumptions.
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Canonical: 'Framing requires thinking about thinking (metacognition)' — planning and monitoring aspects enable effective frame selection and evaluation.
admission_edge.source_description: Metacognitive-questioning gives problem-framing-and-reframing the self-inspection needed to notice when the current lens is producing weak answers.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When deliberate rational analysis would override the emotional and reference-dependent heuristics that PT describes as driving actual behavior.
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Canonical: 'PT stands against the notion that implementation or persuasion is a fundamentally rational process solved via logical, step-by-step methods' — hot cognition vs cold cognition.
admission_edge.source_description: Critical-thinking counters prospect-theory distortions by forcing a colder review of whether the frame is changing the choice more than the fundamentals are.
Prospect-theory conflicts with anchoring when reference-point dependence means the same objective outcome is evaluated differently depending on the arbitrary anchor that sets the gain/loss boundary.

admission_edge.activation_condition: When incentive structures must account for loss aversion and reference-dependent evaluation of outcomes.
admission_edge.affinity_rationale: Moderate: PT describes how loss aversion and reference dependence affect incentive design. Understanding PT is necessary for designing effective behavioral incentives.
admission_edge.source_description: Incentives interact with prospect-theory because gain and loss framing can change behavior without changing the underlying economics.
